historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY26 guidance and the post-Vocus continuing-operations trajectory (continuing revenue +2.8% FY25, -0.9% H1 FY26; service revenue +0.5%); historical CAGRs are structurally uninformative for this business (see notes).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (-10.0%) diverges from revenue (-2.4%) and EPS (-3.6%) by more than 30pp, but the divergence is mechanical, not a signal: the A$2,826m capital reduction in Nov-2025 shrank book equity by a quarter, FY25 EPS includes the A$473m pre-tax disposal gain, and the revenue series mixes the divested fibre/EGW business (5,415 in FY22 total vs 5,041 FY25 continuing). None of these CAGRs is used to set the growth path.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs use total reported revenue (FY2022 5,415 -> FY2025 5,041 continuing; FY2020 4,350 -> FY2025 5,041) and therefore straddle the Vocus divestment; FY2020 is also the merger year (Vodafone Hutchison full year + TPG Corp from 13 Jul 2020). Equity CAGRs span the Nov-2025 A$2.8bn capital return. EPS spans the FY22 tower-sale gain and the FY25 disposal gain. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 573, FY2022 284, FY2025 693 (continuing, normalised; see inputs.reported_fcf_note) - the 3yr figure is flattered because FY22 carried peak 5G/Huawei-swap capex of 961. Reported-FCF CAGR FY22->FY25 would read +75% off the A$687m handset-financing inflow; the owner series strips it. None of these is a credible forward growth rate, which is why selected_growth_rate is set from guidance.

scenario_narratives.base: TPG executes the post-Vocus plan roughly as guided: FY26 EBITDA lands inside the A$1,665-1,735m range on revenue that is flat-to-slightly-down (handset revenue keeps shrinking, Home Broadband is flat, mobile service revenue grows low-single-digit on the mid-2026 price rises and the regional MOCN share gains). Margins expand ~2pp over four years from the A$100m real-terms cost-out and mobile operating leverage, with the rest competed away to Telstra/Optus and the MVNOs. Capex steps down to the guided A$550-650m, but the 2028-2032 spectrum renewals cost ~A$1.1bn in lump sums over five years, roughly offsetting the capex saving during that window. Leases (~A$355m/yr for towers, sites and the TAWFA fibre access) are a permanent operating cost. Cash tax is paid at 30% from here on. The Triple Zero investigation ends in a fine of tens of millions, absorbed within the year.
scenario_narratives.bull: The three-player mobile market stays 'constructive': postpaid price rises stick across all carriers, the Optus MOCN keeps delivering above-market subscriber growth and lower churn, business mobile grows high-single-digit, and the brand/plan simplification lifts ARPU mix. EBITDA margin reaches ~38.5% by FY32. The ACMA softens the Dec-2025 spectrum proposal to instalment payments at a lower price (~A$120m/yr), so the capex step-down to ~A$600m flows straight to FCF. The investment-grade balance sheet lets dividends grow in line with the stated policy and the market re-rates TPG toward Telstra's cash-flow multiple. Owner FCF roughly doubles to ~A$1.0bn by FY35.
scenario_narratives.bear: H1 FY26's revenue decline proves to be the trend, not a blip: MVNO and Optus price competition caps mobile ARPU, Home Broadband keeps losing to NBN resellers and Telstra fixed wireless, and FY26 EBITDA misses the guidance floor. Margins drift to 32% as the Vocus separation drags into 2027 and TAWFA service issues add cost. The ACMA adopts the lump-sum, higher-price renewal framework as proposed, costing TPG ~A$1.6bn over FY28-FY32 - about the entire capex saving the Vocus sale was meant to deliver - and the Triple Zero investigation produces a material penalty plus compliance spend. Lease costs are fixed against a shrinking revenue base. FCF stays positive (the business is not distressed) but there is little growth to capitalise, and the dividend-growth policy stalls.

valuation_philosophy.summary: TPG is valued as a mature, capital-intensive domestic mobile operator whose economics were reset by the July-2025 Vocus sale: lower capex and leverage, but a permanent ~A$355m/yr lease bill for infrastructure it used to own and a looming 2028-2032 spectrum renewal cycle that its capex guidance excludes. The house basis charges all three - leases inside EBITDA, spectrum inside capex, SBC in the flows - discounts in AUD at a single 8% WACC across scenarios, and caps the terminal at 15x FCF (~5.9x ex-lease EV/EBITDA-less-leases, below today's ~7.0x). The resulting value is the price of a 2%-growth cash yield, not a re-rating story; the probability weights carry the regulatory asymmetry rather than the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Spectrum renewal cost 2028-2032: every A$500m of additional lump-sum renewal cost is roughly A$0.20/share of value; the base allowance (~A$1.1bn) is an estimate of TPG's share under the ACMA's Dec-2025 proposal, not a disclosed figure.

Lease run-rate: the ~7% of revenue lease charge is anchored on one half-year (H1 FY26 pro-forma A$177m) of the post-TAWFA structure; CPI escalators on a fixed base make it a rising share of revenue in any low-growth path.
Terminal multiple sensitivity: the 15x FCF cap binds in base and bull; a 12x cap (a de-rated telco) removes ~A$0.50/share from base, while uncapped Gordon at 2% would add ~A$0.30.

D&A glide to tax: cash tax is modelled on unlevered EBIT after an ex-ROU D&A line that falls from 21.9% to 13% of revenue; if acquired-intangible amortisation (non-deductible) is larger than assumed, modelled tax is somewhat too high in the early years (conservative).
Competition: a further 1pp of permanent EBITDA margin is worth ~A$0.12/share; the bear case already assumes margins fall back to 32%.

Regulatory penalties: the ACMA Triple Zero investigation is unquantified; Optus (A$12m) and Telstra (A$3m) precedents suggest a one-off, but a larger penalty or remediation programme would hit a single year's FCF.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular ASX close); 52-week range 3.47-5.85, with the high predating the Nov-2025 A$1.61/share capital return.
data_sources.financials: TPG.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, AUD millions) for history; TPG.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt for FY25 continuing-operations income statement (line 6115-6138), D&A split (note 6(e), line 7084-7087), finance costs (note 6(f)), lease note (lines 8383-8407), discontinued operations (note 5, lines 6900-6943), cash flow overview (lines 1456-1477), contributed equity (note 21, line 9077-9082), FY26 outlook (lines 736-781); TPG.AX_HalfYear_H1-FY2026.txt for the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet (lines 511-516, 946-955), directors' report cash flow and financial position (lines 405-440), EPS denominators (lines 1430-1432) and treasury shares (note 14).

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 revenue from continuing operations (Annual FY2025 income statement line 6116). Total FY2025 revenue incl. the divested fibre/EGW business was 5,423 (5,041 + 382 discontinued); FY2024 continuing restated 4,905 vs 5,520 as originally reported. The growth path compounds from the continuing base only.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: weighted-average diluted shares for H1 FY2026 (1,956,414,899; HalfYear H1-FY2026 note 12, line 1432). Cross-check: 1,963,029,400 ordinary shares on issue at 31 Dec 2025 (Annual FY2025 note 21, line 9082) less 9,554,074 treasury shares held by the Employee Incentive Plan Trust at 30 Jun 2026 (H1-FY2026 note 14) = 1,953.5m basic, plus ~2.3m dilutive rights. The count jumped from 1,859m because 103.7m shares were issued under the Nov-2025 Reinvestment Plan (a genuine non-SBC issue, already in the count). Held FLAT going forward: SBC is expensed in the flows and the EIP Trust buys shares on-market to settle rights (A$25m FY25, A$13m H1 FY26), so the flat count is funded.
inputs.net_debt_note: Gross borrowings 1,435 less cash 55 at 30 Jun 2026 (H1-FY2026 balance sheet lines 515/946-954; directors' report states net borrowings A$1,380m). Lease liabilities of 2,747 (165 current + 2,582 non-current) are EXCLUDED because leases are charged as an operating cost in the flows (treatment B). The A$93m handset-receivables subordinated note (investing, FY25) is left out of the bridge: it is working capital of the financing program, not surplus cash.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 continuing-operations FCF normalised for one-offs: group OCF 2,417 less discontinued-ops OCF 170 (note 5) = 2,247; less the A$687m one-off net benefit of initiating the handset receivables financing program in Oct-2025 = 1,560; less continuing cash capex 774 and spectrum payments 28 = 758. The CSV's reported FreeCashFlow of 1,554 (OCF 2,417 - capex 863) carries both the handset benefit and seven months of the divested business and is not a repeatable base. Finance costs (bank AND lease interest) sit in financing on TPG's cash flow statement, so 758 is pre-interest and pre-lease.
inputs.owner_fcf_after_lease_note: last_fcf (693) is pre-lease. Under lease treatment (B) the FY25 continuing lease cash of ~260 (principal 118, line 6384; lease interest 142, note 15 line 8400) is also an operating charge, giving ~433 of unlevered owner FCF on the FY25 lease base. The post-TAWFA run-rate is higher (~A$355m/yr: H1 FY26 pro-forma lease payments 177, up from 170) and that is what lease_cost_pct_path charges, which is why the modelled FY26 owner FCF (~A$480m) sits below last_fcf.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY25 finance income of 46 (note 6(f), line 7094) was earned on the A$4.9bn Vocus proceeds held between 31 Jul and 24 Nov 2025 and does not recur (H1 FY26: 5). TPG is a net borrower, so the usual net-cash rule does not apply; it is stripped because it is non-recurring, not because a cash pile is being added back.
inputs.sbc_source: Annual FY2025 cash flow statement, share-based payments add-back A$19m (FY24: 12); H1 FY2026 A$8m. EquityAwardTaxes nil in every year (rights are settled with Trust-bought shares; no net-share-settlement tax line). SBC is 0.38% of revenue - an SBC-light market, so house and street bases nearly coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: A$25m FY25 'Payments for shares acquired by TPG Employee Incentive Plan Trust' (line 1475), A$13m H1 FY26. No buyback programme; these purchases fund the flat count. The A$2,826m Nov-2025 return of capital and A$167m special dividend were one-off distributions of the Vocus proceeds, not repurchases.
inputs.price_note: Regular ASX close (Friday 6 Nov 2026, 16:10 AEDT). Not an after-hours print. The 52-week high of 5.85 predates the A$1.61/share capital return + special dividend paid 24 Nov 2025, so the top of the range is not like-for-like with today's price.
inputs.guidance_vintage: FY26 guidance issued 27 Feb 2026 (Annual FY2025, lines 736-781), reaffirmed 21 Aug 2026 with the H1 FY26 result.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in AUD, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.4%; ERP 5.5%; equity beta 0.75 for a defensive domestic mobile operator -> cost of equity ~8.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.8% (BBB/BBB investment-grade from S&P and Fitch, achieved after the FY25 A$2.7bn paydown; H1 FY26 bank interest ~A$50m on ~A$1.4bn), 4.1% after 30% tax. Weights on lease-exclusive capital: equity 8,020 (1,956m x A$4.10) / debt 1,380 -> 85/15 -> WACC 7.8%, rounded to 8.0%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios; cyclicality, competition and regulatory risk are priced in the flows and the probability weights, not stacked into the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. TPG's IFRS-16 lease book (A$2,747m at 30 Jun 2026) is network sites, the towers sold to OMERS in 2022 and leased back, and from 1 Aug 2025 the lease component of the 15+10+10-year TAWFA fibre access agreement with Vocus - all ongoing costs of running the network with no realistic end. The full lease cash (principal + interest) is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path (~7.0% of revenue = ~A$355m, the H1 FY26 pro-forma run-rate of 177 per half); lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY25 continuing: 1,260 - 158 = 1,102 = 21.9% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice; and the sanity multiple is lease-exclusive EV against EBITDA less lease cash (FY26: ~9,400 / ~1,345 = 7.0x), never ex-lease EV over post-IFRS-16 EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. TPG has no material non-controlling interests; all flows are attributable to ordinary shareholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year explicit horizon, with the non-US adaptations (AUD WACC, lease treatment B, SBC-light market). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (operating company, non-US, material leases); TPG is an operating telco, not a REIT/bank/holdco, so no other row applies. No prior DCF or memory entry - fresh build. BUSINESS DISCONTINUITY: the July-2025 sale of the fibre network and EGW fixed business to Vocus (A$5.25bn EV) means FY2019-FY2024 reported figures and the FY2020 merger year are not comparable to the continuing business; every forward driver is anchored on FY2025 continuing-operations figures and FY26 guidance, not on blended historicals. CAPEX INCLUDES SPECTRUM: management's capex guidance (A$750m FY26, A$550-650m medium term) explicitly excludes spectrum payments, which are 'large, uneven and periodic' (FY24: 156, FY25: 28). Most of TPG's licences renew 2028-2032 and the ACMA's December-2025 proposal is for higher renewal prices paid as a lump sum ahead of expiry; capex_pct_path therefore adds an explicit spectrum allowance (base ~A$200m/yr over FY28-FY32, ~A$1.1bn total; bear ~A$300m/yr; bull ~A$120m/yr) on top of guided capex. CASH TAX: TPG exhausted its historic revenue losses against the FY25 disposal gain and began paying cash tax (FY25: 48, H1 FY26: 21, ETR 29%); the 30% Australian statutory rate is applied to unlevered EBIT from year 1 (bank interest deductibility lives in the WACC, not the flows). WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture 0 - contract liabilities are flat (~A$310-330m since FY20) and handset receivables now run through the financing program; the FY25 A$687m inflow was the one-off initiation of that program and is excluded from the base. TERMINAL: cap multiple 15x FCF, the lower end of the house range for a structurally slow-growth telco; at WACC 8% / g 2% Gordon (17x) exceeds the cap so the cap binds in base and bull, Gordon (14.4x) binds in bear. Implied terminal ex-lease EV / (EBITDA - lease) is ~5.9x in base vs ~7.0x today, so the model assumes no multiple expansion.

bear.note: FY26 EBITDA 33.0% = A$1,630m, i.e. a small miss of the A$1,665m guidance floor. Spectrum allowance ~A$300m/yr FY28-32 (~A$1.6bn) if the ACMA's lump-sum, higher-price proposal is adopted as framed. Lease % rises because the TAWFA and tower leases are fixed-plus-CPI against a shrinking revenue line. Gordon (1.01/0.07 = 14.4x) binds rather than the 15x cap.

base.growth_note: FY26 -0.5%: H1 was -0.9% (service +0.5%, handsets -9%) and H2 gets the mid-2026 postpaid price rises. FY27-FY30 2.0-2.5%: industry mobile service revenue growth ~4% (UBS/Jarden) diluted by flat Home Broadband and shrinking hardware. Fades to 2.0% = terminal, roughly CPI.
base.ebitda_margin_note: FY26 33.7% = A$1,690m on A$5,016m, inside the A$1,665-1,735m guidance range, just below the midpoint because H1 came in at 33.9% with a soft revenue line. Then +0.3-0.6pp/yr to 36% by FY32: the A$100m real-terms opex programme to FY29 (~2pp) plus mobile operating leverage, partly given back to competition. Post-IFRS-16 margin, before the lease charge.
base.capex_note: Guided capex plus a spectrum allowance. FY26 750 + ~20 spectrum; FY27 ~640 (top of the 550-650 range as guided) + ~40; FY28-FY32 ~600 + ~200/yr for the 2028-2032 licence renewals (~A$1.1bn total, roughly TPG's share of industry renewals on the ACMA's Dec-2025 pricing); FY33+ ~600 + ~140 ongoing spectrum. Terminal 12.5% of revenue.
base.da_note: Ex right-of-use D&A, 21.9% of revenue in FY25 (1,102 / 5,041), glides to 13.0% as merger-era customer-contract amortisation (~A$70m/yr) rolls off and the asset base re-bases to the lower capex run-rate. Terminal D&A ~ capex.

bull.note: Lease % drifts down because lease payments are largely fixed-plus-CPI while revenue grows 3-4%. Spectrum allowance ~A$120m/yr FY28-32 on the assumption the ACMA moves to instalment payments and a lower price. EBITDA 38.5% matches Telstra-mobile-like economics at TPG's smaller scale.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: the single biggest swing factor - 2028-2032 spectrum renewal pricing - sits with one regulator whose latest (Dec-2025) proposal was adverse enough that management criticised it publicly, there is a live ACMA Triple Zero enforcement investigation with fine precedents at both peers, and the first half-year on the new continuing basis showed revenue falling. Bull down to 25%: the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once (industry price discipline holding, MOCN share gains compounding, the A$100m cost-out landing in full, AND a softer spectrum outcome). There is no going-concern or covenant risk (net debt/EBITDA 0.8x vs a 3.75x covenant), which is why bear is not higher.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
